statement_source_and_scope_match: F17 §1 explicitly conjectures smooth global existence even for one reversible reaction, equations (1)–(3). FT17 equations (1.12)–(1.14), Theorem 1.2 and Remark 1.1 specialize to disjoint reactant/product species on a bounded no-flux domain. The smooth-data case is explicit in F17; integer coefficients are the mass-action molecular counts. General positive rate constants are retained as in F17. The finite-time L-infinity continuation criterion is stated in FMT20 proof overview item (1). AKT26 §1.3 supplies current explicit unresolved disjoint-species examples; its periodic setting is identified separately, not attributed to a Neumann theorem.
proposed_statement_text:
Let $I,J,n\ge1$ be integers and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded connected domain with smooth boundary. Consider distinct chemical species undergoing one reversible reaction
$$
\sum_{i=1}^{I}\alpha_i A_i\ \rightleftarrows\ \sum_{j=1}^{J}\beta_j B_j,
\qquad \alpha_i,\beta_j\in\{1,2,\ldots\}.
$$
For concentrations $a=(a_1,\ldots,a_I)$ and $b=(b_1,\ldots,b_J)$, set
$$
R(a,b)=k_+\prod_{i=1}^{I}a_i^{\alpha_i}
       -k_-\prod_{j=1}^{J}b_j^{\beta_j},\qquad k_+,k_->0.
$$
Fix arbitrary constant diffusivities $d_i,e_j>0$ and solve
$$
\partial_t a_i-d_i\Delta a_i=-\alpha_i R(a,b),\qquad
\partial_t b_j-e_j\Delta b_j=\beta_j R(a,b)
$$
in $(0,\infty)\times\Omega$, with $\partial_\nu a_i=\partial_\nu b_j=0$ on the boundary, where $\nu$ is the outward normal. The initial concentrations are arbitrary nonnegative smooth functions on $\overline\Omega$ satisfying these boundary conditions.

Must the unique local nonnegative classical solution extend to every finite time? Equivalently, can finite-time concentration blowup be excluded for every such reaction, domain, set of coefficients and initial state? The required bound is
$$
\sup_{0\le t\le T}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{I}\|a_i(t)\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}
+\sum_{j=1}^{J}\|b_j(t)\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\right)<\infty
\quad\text{for each }T<\infty.
$$
Here classical means continuous to the initial data and continuously differentiable in time and twice in space for positive times, satisfying the equations and boundary conditions pointwise. Bounds may depend on $T$, the data and all coefficients. No upper bound on reaction order, smallness of the initial data, or closeness of diffusivities is assumed. This is the single-reaction, disjoint-species version of the broader chemical reaction-network regularity question; its parameter cases count as one entry.
applied_significance: This models a closed reaction vessel containing diffusing chemical or biochemical species. Forward and backward mass-action rates couple local concentrations, while species move at different rates. A positive answer would justify using the classical concentration equations through any finite observation interval, even for large spatially uneven initial concentrations and higher-order reactions. Integrated mass and entropy estimates alone do not give the pointwise concentration control needed for that conclusion.

closest_existing_or_new_entries.difference: Scalar growing heat equation with a chosen internal control and Dirichlet boundary; asks exact null controllability.
Stochastic scalar heat equation with rough noise coefficient; asks pathwise uniqueness at a Hölder threshold.
Discrete molecular-count Markov chain; asks nonexplosion and positive recurrence.
Spatially homogeneous ODE; assumes a bounded global trajectory and asks asymptotic nonextinction.
Boltzmann kinetic equation in position/velocity variables; asks unconditional uniqueness of entropy-admissible renormalized solutions, not classical continuation of concentration PDEs.

duplicate_review.distinctness_reason: No existing or accepted expansion statement asks classical continuation for this multi-species deterministic diffusion system.
implications_or_equivalences: Finite-time L-infinity continuation and global classical existence are one canonical question.
Do not separately count dimensions, reaction orders, species counts, or a broader restatement of this same continuation gap.

open_status_evidence_summary: F17 explicitly poses the smooth global question. FT17 treats the same disjoint-species no-flux model with renormalized solutions. A23 independently retains the deterministic reversible-reaction gap; AKT26 still identifies high-order deterministic examples as open. P21 and HT26 distinguish known generic mass-control blowup from the entropy-dissipating chemical setting. A16 found no matching later resolution.
independent_status_corroboration: F17, FT17 and A23 have disjoint author lists. AKT26 is also author-disjoint from F17, but overlaps with FT17 and A23; it is not counted as an independent source from those two.
strongest_known_partial_results_and_gap: General entropy-based renormalized existence; classical continuation at quadratic growth and under special diffusion/data/structural assumptions. Arbitrary-order, arbitrary-positive-diffusivity classical continuation remains the target.
